description:
We are a team of five students passionate about space science. We are tackling the challenge to "Identify Earth Locations that Analog Moon and Mars." We have researched sites like the Atacama Desert and Mistastin Crater to see how they mimic space environments.
We need teammates with:
Design skills: To create visual presentations/maps.
Google Earth skills: To plot coordinates.
Passion for space!
Join a motivated team ready to build a great solution for NASA!
summary: Far From Home is a web platform with an interactive 3D map and an educational game that bring Mars to Earth. We answer one question from the challenge: where on Earth can we study Mars, and how close is the match really? Our map pairs China's Qaidam Basin, often called "Mars on Earth", with three Martian sites: Gale Crater, Jezero Crater and the Medusae Fossae Formation. Using NASA imagery, elevation data and published evidence, it compares 17 features and rates each one Strong, Partial, Different or Not yet measured, with sources. In our game, Planet Detective: Mission 2077, players explore Qaidam on foot, report to Mission Control and drive a rover on Mars. This matters because every Mars mission is tested on Earth first: our platform shows what can and cannot be tested at each site, and lets students learn planetary science by doing it.
details:
What it does

Far From Home answers one question: where on Earth can we study Mars, and how close is the match really? It has three parts on one website:

1. Interactive 3D map: Earth and Mars globes side by side. Users pick an Earth site and its Mars twin; both globes zoom in and the platform shows the data for both.

2. Evidence matrix: 17 features compared across 3 site pairs, each rated Strong, Partial, Different or Not yet measured, with numbered sources.

3. Planet Detective: Mission 2077: an educational 3D game. Players walk the Qaidam salt crust with field instruments (camera, spectrometer, thermal infrared, LiDAR, ground-penetrating radar, probe), report to Mission Control, then drive the ARES-6 rover on Mars and scan its terrain. Mars readings in the game are simulated and labelled as such.

Analog pairs

- Wusute Yardang field ↔ Medusae Fossae Formation: wind-carved yardangs in soft sediment

- Dalangtan Playa ↔ Gale Crater: salts and clays left by drying water

- Qarhan Salt Lake ↔ Jezero Crater: ancient lakes that dried out

Our own measurements

Using NASA Viking MDIM2.1 imagery we measured yardang orientation in Medusae Fossae on 4 fields: 151° (range 139–161°). We also measured terrain relief and slope at every site with the same method on both planets (AWS Terrain Tiles for Earth, NASA MOLA for Mars).

How it works and tools

Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The globes use three.js with relief exaggerated 10×; the game uses React Three Fiber and is hosted on Vercel. The map is bilingual (Arabic and English).

Live site: https://phoniexteam52-lgtm.github.io/NASA-Far-From-Home/

Game: https://cis-phoenix.vercel.app/

Code: https://github.com/phoniexteam52-lgtm/NASA-Far-From-Home

Benefits and intended impact

Students learn planetary geology by exploring, not memorizing. Mission teams get a clear list of what can and cannot be tested at each Earth analog. Every claim links to its source, so anyone can check it.

How it is creative

Instead of one "Mars-like place", we rate every feature separately and show where the match fails, then turn that research into a playable mission: the same evidence a student reads on the map, they collect themselves in the game.

Factors we considered

Scientific honesty (every claim sourced, simulated game data labelled), access for students (free, browser-based, Arabic and English), and testing value (what can and cannot be tested at each site).

Next steps

Measure yardang size on Mars with sharper CTX images, add more Earth analog sites, and build a classroom kit around the game chapters.

SI use: our demo video's voiceover was generated with AI text-to-speech and its motion graphics were made with AI assistance; the video carries a visible SI label.

Team CIS Phoenix, Cairo, Egypt: Ahmed Abdelrahman (team lead); Ziad Ahmed Fattouh and Omar Mostafa Mohammed (map); Yara Ibrahim Adel, Malak Mohamed Elarieny and Shaza Osama Altantawy (game).
